name: Roslindale
headline: A 1911 substation on the square,
the Needham Line and the Arboretum's Peters Hill.
answer: Roslindale is a Boston neighborhood about six miles south-southwest of downtown, between the Arnold Arboretum and the George Wright Golf Course, and was part of the town of West Roxbury until annexation to Boston took effect in 1874. One- and two-family houses make up much of its housing, with newer apartment buildings around Roslindale Square. The Boston Planning & Development Agency counted 29,386 people there in 2020, and the Needham Line stops at Roslindale Village.
meta: Roslindale, Boston: one- and two-family houses around Roslindale Square, the Needham Line at Roslindale Village, and the Arnold Arboretum's Peters Hill.

boundaries.text: Boston's open space plan notes that Roslindale's edges are not distinct, but describes the planning district as bounded by the Arnold Arboretum and the Walter Street Tract to the north, the former Boston State Hospital campus and the Forest Hills and Mount Hope cemeteries to the east, the West Roxbury Parkway to the west, and the George Wright Golf Course and part of the Stony Brook Reservation to the south. Jamaica Plain, Hyde Park, West Roxbury and Mattapan are its neighbors.

overview: Roslindale was part of the town of Roxbury until 1851, when it, Jamaica Plain and West Roxbury left Roxbury to form the town of West Roxbury. The Boston and Providence Railroad opened its West Roxbury Branch from Forest Hills to Dedham on July 14, 1849, with a station at South Street, and by the 1860s the area was known as South Street Crossing. When residents sought their own post office district, the Postal Service rejected that name, and John Pierce proposed Roslindale, after Roslin, near Edinburgh. Voters approved annexation to Boston in 1873, and it took effect in 1874. Horse-drawn street railway service between Forest Hills and Dedham followed in the 1880s.

Washington Street is the neighborhood's commercial spine and runs through Roslindale Square, which took its present layout in the 1920s around Adams Park. Beside the square stands the Roslindale Substation, built by the Boston Elevated Railway in 1911 to a design by Robert S. Peabody and listed on the National Register in 2013. In 1929 Ashland Street was widened and renamed Cummins Highway, from Washington Street to River Street. Roslindale Village Main Street, established in 1985 as one of the first urban Main Street programs in the country, runs the farmers' market and events in the square. To the north, the part of the Arnold Arboretum south of Bussey Street, including Peters Hill, at 240 feet, lies in Roslindale, and rail lines divide the neighborhood roughly into thirds.

Boston's 2008-2014 open space plan counted one- and two-family houses as 60% of Roslindale's housing, against 32% citywide; the western streets resemble West Roxbury, while the northern streets mix two- and three-family houses with light industrial buildings. Roslindale Square was the first plan adopted under the city's Squares + Streets initiative: the planning process ran from February 2024 to February 2025, the Boston Planning & Development Agency board adopted the Roslindale Square Small Area Plan on February 13, 2025, and the Zoning Commission approved new zoning in May 2025, effective June 2, 2025. It was the second area of the city with Squares + Streets districts in force, and the zoning allows multifamily housing near and above ground-floor businesses.

housing.text: Roslindale is mostly one- and two-family houses: Boston's 2008-2014 open space plan put single-family homes at 33% and two-family homes at 27% of units, 60% together, compared with 32% citywide. Its western streets are mainly one- and two-family houses, its northern streets have more two- and three-family houses, and newer apartment buildings stand around Roslindale Square. The Boston Planning & Development Agency's tabulation of the 2016-2020 American Community Survey counts 53.8% of occupied units as owner-occupied (6,539 units), compared with 35.3% citywide.

areas.name: Roslindale Square
areas.line: The business district around Adams Park, where Washington Street runs through the square, with Roslindale Village station at 1 Belgrade Avenue, the 1911 Roslindale Substation and the Squares + Streets zoning adopted in 2025.

areas.name: The Arboretum edge
areas.line: The northern side, where the part of the Arnold Arboretum south of Bussey Street, including 240-foot Peters Hill, lies within Roslindale; the 1887 Bussey Street bridge collapse took place on what is now Arboretum land.

areas.name: Cummins Highway
areas.line: Formerly Ashland Street, widened to 60 to 80 feet and renamed in 1929; it runs from Washington Street to River Street and was the first road in Boston called a highway.

commute.text: Roslindale Village station, at 1 Belgrade Avenue in the square, is on the Needham Line, which runs through Forest Hills, Ruggles and Back Bay to South Station; Forest Hills, in Jamaica Plain, connects with the Orange Line. Ten MBTA bus routes run on Washington Street between Forest Hills and Roslindale Square and fan out to the south and west. The West Roxbury Parkway runs along the western edge.

places.name: Roslindale Substation
places.line: A 1911 Boston Elevated Railway substation at 4228 Washington Street, designed by Robert S. Peabody of Peabody and Stearns and listed on the National Register on August 27, 2013; the city sold it in 2013 to Historic Boston Incorporated and Roslindale Village Main Street, and its ground floor opened as a beer hall in spring 2022.

places.name: Adams Park
places.line: The green at the center of Roslindale Square, renovated by the city with a performance space, walkways and landscaping, where the Saturday farmers' market is held.

places.name: Arnold Arboretum and Peters Hill
places.line: Harvard's 281-acre arboretum, founded in 1872 and open free every day, lies in Jamaica Plain and Roslindale; Peters Hill, at 240 feet the tallest of its hills, is in the Roslindale section.

places.name: Roslindale Wetlands
places.line: A city urban wild, once called the Eldon Street Urban Wild, with a wetland, woodland and meadow, a perimeter loop trail built in improvements between 2020 and 2024, and entrances on Walter Street, Weld Street, Hazelmere Road and Coniston Road.

places.name: Healy Playground and Fallon Field
places.line: City recreation grounds: Healy Playground has three ball fields and a stairway from Washington Street, and Fallon Field has a playground and basketball courts.

places.name: George Wright Golf Course
places.line: An 18-hole municipal course designed by Donald Ross and opened on April 23, 1938, at 420 West Street; it lies in Hyde Park and Roslindale and marks Roslindale's southern edge.

history.text: The Boston and Providence Railroad's West Roxbury Branch opened on July 14 with a station at South Street, today's Roslindale Village station.
Annexation to Boston took effect, after voters in the town of West Roxbury, which included Roslindale, approved it in 1873.
On March 14, a railroad bridge at Bussey Street collapsed under a train carrying more than 200 passengers, killing 23; the site is now in the Arnold Arboretum.
The Roslindale Square Small Area Plan, the first plan adopted under Squares + Streets, was adopted on February 13, and its zoning took effect on June 2.

A guide built from city, MBTA and Warren Group sources can fill that gap.

faq.q: What is the median home price in Roslindale?
faq.a: According to The Warren Group's MA December 2025 Sales, Prices by Town table, which lists Roslindale on its own row, the median single-family sale price for calendar year 2025 was $778,000, across 86 sales, up from $762,000 across 96 sales in 2024. The condominium median was $615,000 across 106 sales in 2025, against $590,000 across 95 sales in 2024.
Yes. The MBTA Needham Line stops at Roslindale Village, at 1 Belgrade Avenue in Roslindale Square, and runs through Forest Hills, Ruggles and Back Bay to South Station.
Boston Public Schools. School assignment is set by the district; review its profile with DESE.

faq.q: What is Squares + Streets zoning in Roslindale Square?
faq.a: Roslindale Square was the first area to have a plan adopted under Boston's Squares + Streets initiative, on February 13, 2025. Its zoning, effective June 2, 2025, allows mixed-use development and multifamily housing near and above ground-floor businesses.

faq.q: Is the Arnold Arboretum in Roslindale?
faq.a: Partly. The arboretum's 281 acres lie in Jamaica Plain and Roslindale, and the section south of Bussey Street, including Peters Hill, is in Roslindale.

notes: Written 2026-10-23. Population: Boston Planning & Development Agency Research Division, 'Boston in Context: Neighborhoods, 2020 Decennial Census Redistricting Data and 2016-2020 American Community Survey' (April 2022), 'Population by Age Group' table, total 29,386 (the same report and neighborhood approximation used for West Roxbury and Jamaica Plain); tenure 53.8% owner-occupied, 6,539 owner-occupied units, Boston 35.3%, from its Housing Tenure table. The total number of occupied units was not read, so it is not given. Housing shares (33% single-family, 27% two-family, 60% together, 32% citywide) and the boundary description are from Boston's Open Space Plan 2008-2014, section 7.2.11 Roslindale (Boston Parks & Recreation; assumed to be the same 2008-2014 plan as the West Roxbury section because of the file series), which rests on older census data and is dated; that plan's 47% owner-occupied figure was not used in favor of the 2022 BPDA figure. The plan also gives 496 acres of protected open space (812 acres total inventory); not used in copy. The one- and two-family western streets, two- and three-family northern streets and newer apartment buildings around the square are from Wikipedia's Roslindale article. History: 1851 secession, South Street Crossing, the name from Roslin, Scotland (proposed by John Pierce), the 1873 annexation vote, 1880s horse railway, the March 14, 1887 Bussey Street bridge collapse, the 1920s square layout and the 1929 Cummins Highway renaming are from Wikipedia's Roslindale article; the 1874 effective date of annexation is from the West Roxbury record (Wikipedia, January 5, 1874). Wikipedia's Roslindale infobox gives an annexation date of September 16, 1873, which conflicts; the copy says voters approved annexation in 1873 and it took effect in 1874. Station: 1 Belgrade Ave (MBTA stop page https://www.mbta.com/stops/place-NB-0064, which also lists a 143-space lot; prices left out because they can change); July 14, 1849 opening as South Street, 1876 brick station and ten bus routes (Wikipedia's Roslindale Village station article, which lists routes 14, 30, 34, 34E, 35, 36, 37, 40, 50 and 51; route numbers are left out of the copy because the MBTA bus network is being redesigned). Squares + Streets: the planning page (http://www.bostonplans.org/planning-zoning/planning-initiatives/roslindale-square) gives the process as February 2024 to February 2025, BPDA board plan adoption February 13, 2025, zoning map and text amendments approved by the board April 10, 2025, Zoning Commission adoption May 21, 2025 and effective date June 2, 2025 (Article 67, Maps 10A and 10B). The city news release 'Zoning Commission approves new Squares + Streets zoning in Roslindale Square' (https://boston.gov/news/zoning-commission-approves-new-squares-streets-zoning-roslindale-square, published May 22, 2025) says the commission 'today approved' it and that Roslindale is 'the second area of the city where Squares + Streets zoning districts are now implemented'; because the two city pages differ by a day (May 21 vs May 22), the copy says May 2025. The Boston city record uses May 22, 2025. The February 14, 2025 city news release calls it 'the first Squares + Streets plan adopted' (https://www.boston.gov/node/16354006). Substation: Wikipedia (1911, Peabody, 4228 Washington Street, NRHP August 27, 2013, 2013 sale, 2022 beer hall); the operator is not named because business details can change. Roslindale Village Main Street founding 1985 from https://www.roslindale.net/about-us; its Great American Main Street Award year was not confirmed and is left out. Arboretum: 281 acres, 1872, free daily (https://arboretum.harvard.edu/about/); Jamaica Plain and Roslindale location and Peters Hill 240 feet (Wikipedia); 'south of Bussey Street' is from Wikipedia's Roslindale article. Adams Park, Healy Playground and Fallon Field: city news page from about 2015 (https://content.boston.gov/node/23351); acreages not given; the direct boston.gov park pages failed to load. Roslindale Wetlands acreage was not given on the city page. George Wright Golf Course from Wikipedia (420 West Street, Donald Ross, April 23, 1938, 18 holes, Hyde Park and Roslindale). Highway names are local streets and parkways named in the sources; no route numbers were confirmed. Schools: assignment is by address and set by Boston Public Schools; no individual school is named. Wikipedia lists schools in Roslindale, but none were checked against BPS. Nearby: West Roxbury, Jamaica Plain, Hyde Park and Mattapan are the neighbors named by Wikipedia. Market: values from tools/data/boston-neighborhood-rows-2025.json (Warren Group rows read 2026-10-23 with pdf.js; single reading, so no reading_2); 96 to 86 sales is -10.4% and $762,000 to $778,000 is 2.1%, matching the row. Region: set to 'Greater Boston' as instructed for this round; the earlier Boston neighborhood records use 'Greater Boston (the city)'. Fair housing: Wikipedia's 2020 race and ethnicity breakdown, its 'garden suburb' nickname, its description of the square's decline with vacant storefronts and vandalism, and its notable-residents list were left out. 'Streetcar suburb' (open space plan, Wikipedia) was also left out in favor of the dated horse-railway fact. Fire, police and EMS station details were left out.
